name: Shankara Buildpro Ltd
title: Shankara Buildpro Ltd - 544517 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 steel volume up 27% to 3.03 lakh tonnes with EBITDA margin 3.39%, below the 3.5% floor; management reiterated 1.2 million tonne and 20% steel growth targets and 3.5% steady-state margin, with no capacity capex (asset-light marketplace), so supply signal is neutral.

summary.headline: Shankara Buildpro Q2 FY27 revenue rose 43% YoY to Rs 2,280 crore and PAT 57% to Rs 46.2 crore, but EBITDA margin stayed near 3.4%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with steel volume up 27% YoY to 3.03 lakh tons. EBITDA margin was 3.39%, which management attributed to competitive pressure, new-market entry and higher marketing spend in a seasonally weak quarter. Non-steel revenue reached Rs 181 crore (up 17% YoY, 10% QoQ), and working capital fell to 22 days. The call was held shortly after the death of founder and MD Sukumar Srinivas on October 30, 2026, with Dhananjay Mirlay Srinivas appointed MD on November 1, 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up from 35% in Q1 and 36% in FY26

segments.name: Steel marketplace
segments.commentary: Core growth engine; volume 3.03 lakh tons (up 27% YoY) and revenue Rs 2,100 crore (up 46% YoY). Growth across tubes, flats and roofing in both retail and non-retail channels. Management gave a product mix of about 25% tubes, 50% flats, and the rest longs, CMTs and roofing.

segments.name: Non-steel marketplace
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 181 crore, up 17% YoY and 10% QoQ, the second consecutive quarter of growth; H1 growth about 16%. Management puts non-steel EBITDA near 5% versus 2.5-3% for steel.

segments.name: Western region
segments.commentary: Western India was about 5% of top line a few years ago and is now about 20% of revenue and volume, per management.

guidance_outlook: Steel volume target of about 1.2 million tons for FY27, with management saying it remains on track; analyst cited 1.45 million tons for FY28.
Steel volume growth of about 20% and non-steel value growth of about 20-25% expected going forward.
Steady-state EBITDA margin of about 3.5%; aspiration of about 4% within 2-3 years through better steel product mix, higher volumes and non-steel growth.
Non-steel to rise to about 12-15% of revenue in 2-3 years.
Store additions of about 8 in FY27 versus a steady state of about 5 per year; 3 more stores or fulfilment centres in pipeline; store count 134 after 5 additions in H1.
Working capital guided at 30 days as steady state despite 22 days in Q2.
Non-steel revenue of Rs 1,000 crore is achievable with existing stores, per management, beyond which new territories or stores would be needed.
capex_capacity: Store capex about Rs 2.5-3 crore for a 4,000-5,000 sq ft store; average payback 4-5 years; mature store EBITDA about 4%; breakeven 1.5-2 years.
New fulfilment centre in Jaipur, Rajasthan and a new store in Nanded, Maharashtra added in Q2; 134 stores and fulfilment centres in total.
FY27 store openings planned at about 8; one store in Kerala to be converted into a hybrid store as the only non-steel expansion this year.
Management says it will hold off on new states for about 3 years and focus on deepening existing states.
demand_pricing: Q2 was seasonally soft, and management said the company was more aggressive on marketing to stay competitive, which compressed margins.
Management attributed Q2 steel volume growth to network reach, government infrastructure spending, steel structures demand, promotion, and a wider flats and roofing range.

Management said steel price moves netted out in Q2 (September spike offset by flat or lower earlier months), so no material inventory gain or loss. In Q1, falling steel prices caused about a 10% hit on inventory value, per management.
Dealer financing covered about Rs 15 crore of receivables in Q2, with management saying no real margin impact.
Management said retail and non-retail split is about 50:50, but declined to give detailed customer-type data.
Management said Q2 payables were pressured in September and supplier support helped keep payables manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not improve despite strong steel volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited competition and new-market entry; it was more aggressive on marketing in the seasonally subdued Q2, causing margin contraction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1.2 million ton volume target still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said it remains on track, though the founder's passing was an unfortunate event.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 3.5% is steady state; aspiration is about 4% within 2-3 years, balancing marketing spend and territory expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the western states relative to the south?
qa_highlights.answer: Western region has grown from about 5% to about 20% of revenue and volume, with management saying there is still a lot of runway and the south will remain more established.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex Rs 2.5-3 crore per store of 4,000-5,000 sq ft; payback 4-5 years; mature store EBITDA about 4%; breakeven 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can working capital go lower than 22 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would guide to 30 days as the steady state, with Q2's 22 days a remarkable outcome of the finance team's efforts.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from marketing spend in new states (Rajasthan, west) and whether EBITDA margin moves toward 3.5% steady state.

Steel price volatility: management admitted a roughly 10% inventory hit in Q1 when prices fell, and the company cannot fully pass through price moves given quarterly fixed pricing in consumer markets.
Working capital reverting from 22 days toward the stated 30-day steady state.
Leadership transition after the founder's death; execution of the FY27 volume target of 1.2 million tons.
Management declined to share retail or homeowner data and has moved to steel and non-steel reporting, reducing visibility on channel mix.
Shareholder request for buybacks rather than dividends; board to discuss, no decision announced.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and volume targets, but cautious on margins, which management said would improve only gradually. Tone was respectful and sombre about the founder's death, with some evasiveness on customer-mix and detailed store data.
key_quotes: In Q2 FY27, we delivered Buildpro's highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
It's a mix of the competition in the market and entering new markets.
So non-steel currently is around a 5% EBITDA for us, whereas steel is around 2.5% to 3%.
Yes. 3.5, this is our steady-state is what we are looking to.

adds.what: New fulfilment centre in Jaipur, Rajasthan and new store in Nanded, Maharashtra added in Q2 (134 stores and fulfilment centres in total)
FY27 store openings of about 8 (3 more stores or fulfilment centres in pipeline; 5 added in H1)

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 steel volume target of about 1.2 million tons (H1 at 5.53 lakh tons) and steel volume growth of about 20% plus non-steel value growth of 20-25%, backed partly by about 8 store openings in FY27 (134 stores after H1 additions) and demand drivers, though no detailed order or capacity numbers were given for the full-year volume target.

mgmt.note: Founder and MD Sukumar Srinivas died on October 30, 2026; Dhananjay Mirlay Srinivas appointed MD on November 1, 2026, with no stated growth plan beyond reiterating FY27 targets.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 3.39% in Q2 vs a 3.5% steady state and a 4% aspiration in 2-3 years, but management is spending more on marketing to compete, so gains will be gradual.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 8 store openings are planned in FY27 (5 added in H1, 3 more in pipeline) at about Rs 2.5-3 crore each, against a steady state of about 5 a year.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reaffirmed about 20% steel volume growth and the 1.2 million ton FY27 target, with H1 at 5.53 lakh tons (up 19% YoY); the H2 run-rate needed is not spelled out.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, and management plans to stay within existing states for about 3 years, so there is no sign of a major new plant; only store capex is planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is guiding to a 3.5% steady-state margin and is spending more on marketing, so it has not signalled any raise to guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management admits a Q2 margin squeeze from competition, the founder's death has created a leadership transition, and 1.2 million ton delivery needs a strong H2 after H1 at 5.53 lakh tons.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Non-steel is growing 17% YoY to Rs 181 crore, and the non-steel target is Rs 1,000 crore on existing stores, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Western India scale-up (about 20% of revenue)
rows.why: Western region has grown from about 5% to about 20% of revenue and volume, with management saying there is still a lot of runway, though it also adds marketing cost in new states.

rows.label: Working capital reverting to 30 days
rows.why: Q2 was 22 days vs a 30-day steady-state guide, so the working capital gain is expected to reverse.

rows.label: Buyback request from shareholders
rows.why: A shareholder asked for buybacks instead of dividends and the board will discuss it, but no decision has been announced.

tone.note: Management was confident on the quarter, the 1.2 million ton volume target and store growth, but cautious on margins, which it said would improve only gradually, and evasive on customer mix and store data. Analysts pushed on why margins did not improve despite strong volumes.
